title: Most haunted places in Georgia
excerpt: Georgia’s 10 most haunted places, from Rhodes Hall in Atlanta to Savannah’s historic inns. Discover chilling ghost stories and local legends.
content:
• Georgia's haunted sites range from Victorian hotels and Civil War-era buildings to historic theaters and cemeteries spanning centuries.
  • Paranormal reports include unexplained footsteps, mysterious figures, cold spots, and apparitions reported by visitors and staff members.
  • These locations attract tourists seeking to combine authentic historical exploration with local folklore and ghost-story traditions.

1. Rhodes Hall – Atlanta, Georgia

One of Atlanta’s most recognizable historic mansions, Rhodes Hall has earned a reputation as one of Georgia’s most intriguing haunted locations.

Built between 1902 and 1904 for furniture magnate Amos Rhodes, the impressive granite mansion is often called the “Castle on Peachtree.” Its elaborate architecture, stained-glass windows, and grand staircase make it a remarkable landmark even before the ghost stories begin.

According to reported accounts, staff members and tour guests have experienced unexplained footsteps on the second floor. Others have described seeing mysterious figures in mirrors or noticing artwork that appeared to move without explanation.

Rhodes Hall is now associated with the Georgia Trust for Historic Preservation, and its history makes it an appealing destination for anyone interested in Atlanta’s past.

Why visit: Explore an architectural landmark with a fascinating history and a reputation for unexplained encounters.

2. Mercer-Williams House – Savannah, Georgia

Savannah is famous for its historic streets and ghost stories, and the Mercer-Williams House remains one of its most talked-about landmarks.

Located on Monterey Square, this elegant historic residence gained widespread attention through the book and film Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil. The property is closely associated with antiques dealer Jim Williams and the widely publicized 1981 shooting death of Danny Hansford.

Over the years, stories about the house have included reports of unexplained cold spots and sightings of figures believed by some visitors to resemble former occupants.

Its combination of architectural beauty, Southern Gothic atmosphere, and a complicated history has helped cement its place in Savannah’s folklore.

Why visit: Discover one of Savannah’s best-known historic homes and the real-life events behind its enduring mystique.

Visitor note: Access to historic interiors may be restricted to scheduled tours or specific visitor arrangements.

3. Fox Theatre – Atlanta, Georgia

The Fox Theatre is one of Atlanta’s most beloved entertainment landmarks, but its history also includes a collection of ghost stories.

Opened in 1929, the theater is celebrated for its lavish design, elaborate ceilings, and ornate interiors inspired by architectural traditions from around the world.

Despite its glamorous appearance, the Fox has become associated with reports of strange footsteps, mysterious figures, and unexplained sounds. One recurring legend involves a former boiler-room worker known as Roosevelt, who is said to linger around the building.

These stories have contributed to the theater’s appeal among paranormal enthusiasts, particularly during Halloween season.

Of course, the Fox Theatre is more than a haunted attraction. It remains a major venue for concerts, stage productions, and special events.

Why visit: Experience one of Atlanta’s architectural treasures while learning about the legends surrounding its long history.

4. Windsor Hotel – Americus, Georgia

In downtown Americus, the Windsor Hotel stands as an impressive reminder of Georgia’s Victorian-era elegance.

Opened in 1892, the hotel was designed to accommodate travelers seeking comfortable accommodations in the South. Its distinctive towers, grand balconies, and historic interior give the building a character that feels especially atmospheric after dark.

The Windsor is also associated with several ghost stories. Popular local legends describe sightings of a young girl believed to have died in an elevator accident and reports involving Floyd Lowery, a longtime doorman whose spirit is said to remain connected to the property.

Visitors and paranormal enthusiasts have also described unexplained cold spots and mysterious apparitions.

Whether these accounts are supernatural or simply part of the hotel’s folklore, the Windsor remains a memorable destination for travelers interested in historic Georgia.

Why visit: Admire Victorian architecture and discover the stories attached to one of Americus’s most recognizable landmarks.

5. Waverly Hall Cemetery – Waverly Hall, Georgia

For those who find cemeteries both peaceful and mysterious, Waverly Hall Cemetery offers a glimpse into Georgia’s past.

The historic burial ground dates to the early 19th century and contains graves connected to different periods of the region’s history, including the Civil War era.

Like many old cemeteries, Waverly Hall has developed a reputation for unexplained activity. Paranormal accounts have included sightings of shadowy figures and unusual experiences among the graves.

The age of the cemetery, its historic markers, and its quiet surroundings create an atmosphere that naturally lends itself to ghost stories.

However, reported sightings remain unverified, and the cemetery should be approached first and foremost as a place of remembrance.

Why visit: Learn about local history and explore the stories surrounding one of Georgia’s older burial grounds.

Visitor note: Check local access rules before visiting, and always respect graves, private property, and posted restrictions.

6. Kennesaw House – Marietta, Georgia

Marietta’s Kennesaw House is another Georgia landmark where history and haunting legends intersect.

Originally constructed in 1845 as a cotton warehouse, the building later operated as a hotel. During the Civil War, it was associated with military activity and served as a hospital during a turbulent period in the region’s history.

Today, the building is connected to the Marietta History Center and helps tell the story of the city and its past.

Its history has also inspired reports of paranormal encounters. Legends associated with the property include a mysterious elevator, a ghostly surgeon, and a spirit said to resemble a former resident known as Mrs. Fletcher.

For visitors, the appeal lies in the combination of documented historical events and the unexplained stories that have accumulated over time.

Why visit: Explore Marietta’s history and learn about the Civil War-era stories associated with one of its historic buildings.

7. Margaret Mitchell House – Atlanta, Georgia

Literary history meets paranormal folklore at the Margaret Mitchell House in Atlanta.

The home is best known as the place where author Margaret Mitchell wrote much of her celebrated novel Gone with the Wind. The property offers a connection to one of the most influential works in American popular literature.

Over the years, the house has also attracted stories about unusual occurrences. Some legends suggest that Mitchell’s presence can still be felt around the property, while other accounts refer to strange events reported by people connected to the building.

The house’s history includes a 1977 séance reported in connection with its paranormal lore, adding another layer to its reputation.

While there is no verified evidence that the author’s spirit remains there, the combination of literary significance and local legends makes the site an intriguing stop for visitors.

Why visit: Explore the legacy of a famous Georgia author while discovering the mysterious stories associated with her former home.

8. Pirate’s House – Savannah, Georgia

Few places combine history, atmosphere, and ghost stories quite like the Pirate’s House in Savannah.

The historic establishment traces its origins to the 18th century and has long been associated with maritime history, sailors, and colorful pirate legends. Its rustic interiors and old-fashioned atmosphere make it a memorable stop for anyone exploring Savannah.

Stories about the property include tales of wandering spirits, mysterious activity, and connections to sailors who supposedly passed through its doors centuries ago.

The Pirate’s House has become a popular destination for visitors who want to pair a meal with a little local folklore.

Although the stories surrounding the building vary, its historic character provides a genuine connection to Savannah’s past.

Why visit: Enjoy a distinctive historic setting while learning about the maritime legends and ghost stories associated with Savannah.

9. Lustrat House – Athens, Georgia

Athens is best known for its university, music scene, and cultural attractions, but the city also has a place in Georgia’s haunted history.

The Lustrat House is associated with reports of unexplained presences and apparitions, including accounts said to date back to before the Civil War.

Some paranormal reports connected to the property describe the feeling that someone is nearby even when no one can be seen. Other accounts refer to mysterious figures.

These stories have helped establish the house as one of the locations of interest for people who enjoy investigating Georgia’s lesser-known ghost legends.

As with other reportedly haunted properties, the stories are part of local paranormal lore rather than proof of supernatural activity.

Why visit: Discover a lesser-known part of Georgia’s haunted history outside the state’s better-known paranormal destinations.

Visitor note: Confirm whether the property is open to the public before planning a visit.

10. Hamilton-Turner Inn – Savannah, Georgia

Rounding out the list is the Hamilton-Turner Inn, one of Savannah’s best-known historic accommodations.

Located on Lafayette Square, this striking mansion was built in 1873 and is admired for its elaborate architecture and historic character. Today, it operates as an inn, allowing guests to experience a historic Savannah setting firsthand.

The property has also developed a reputation for paranormal activity. Reports have included mysterious voices and sightings of apparitions, with accounts circulating for decades.

Its location in Savannah’s historic district makes it especially appealing to travelers interested in combining historic sightseeing with the city’s ghost-tour culture.

Even without a supernatural encounter, the building offers a memorable example of the architecture and atmosphere that make Savannah such a popular destination.

Why visit: Experience a historic Savannah property associated with decades of ghost stories and reports of unexplained encounters.

Visitor note: Check the inn’s current policies and availability before planning an overnight stay.

Would you dare to visit one of Georgia’s most haunted places after dark?

Editorial note: Paranormal claims in this article are presented as reported stories and local folklore, not verified facts. Historical access, tour schedules, and admission policies can change; check with each property before visiting.
